sources.label: Europe PMC full text (results, discussion, methods, data and code availability)

ingestion.notes: Supplementary notes and data files were not read.

enhanced_abstract.tldr: A multi-agent LLM system that annotates clusters, checks itself, scores its own confidence and explains its reasoning; across 970 cell types it beat existing methods by 12–41% in fully correct annotations, and it does notably well on cancer cells and fine T cell states.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Single-prompt LLM annotation (e.g. GPTCelltype) can hallucinate, gives every answer with the same confidence, doesn't explain itself, and uses few markers, so it struggles with subpopulations.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.body: Five core agents: an Annotator (zero-shot chain-of-thought, mimicking an expert's workflow), a Validator that checks marker–cell type consistency and sends failures back to the Annotator, a Formatter, a Quality Scorer (0–100), and a Reporter that writes a full reasoning report. Optional agents: Annotation Boost (re-examines low-scoring calls using the full FindAllMarkers table), Subclustering (annotates all subclusters of one population together), Consensus Similarity (agreement across repeated runs) and a RAG agent (CellMarker 2.0 markers plus Cell Ontology trees).

sections.heading: Inputs
sections.body: Species, tissue, and per-cluster markers, typically from Seurat FindAllMarkers or Scanpy rank_genes_groups. The top 50 markers worked best; accuracy plateaus after that. Clustering is done beforehand by the user.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: On GTEx, Tabula Sapiens, Human Cell Landscape, Mouse Cell Atlas and Azimuth it raised fully correct annotations by 12–41% and fully-or-partially correct by 9–20% over the next-best method. In cancer data it found 72.5% of cancer cells (vs. 20% for GPTCelltype), rising to 88–100% with one extra prompt line, and it recognized brain metastases from lung primaries. On PBMC68k and the ProjecTILs T cell reference it improved accuracy by 27% and was the only method that consistently separated naive, memory and exhausted T cells.

sections.heading: Confidence and error-checking
sections.body: Quality scores below 75 mostly flagged wrong or partial calls; scores above 90 were mostly correct. Annotation Boost fixed 24 of 27 low-scoring wrong calls without breaking correct ones. High-confidence disagreements also exposed likely errors in gold-standard labels (e.g. 'monocytes' that express Schwann cell markers).

key_findings: Self-validation plus a confidence score lets users tell low-quality annotations from good ones
Works across underlying models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.92, GPT-4o 0.88, LLaMA-3.2-90B 0.82 on a 100-cell-type benchmark
Detects mixed clusters (90% in 50:50 simulations) and cancer cells far better than single-prompt LLMs
About $0.02 per annotation with GPT-4o; ~2 minutes for 20 clusters on 8 cores
limitations: Depends on marker quality; weaker on continuous developmental data (0.53 average accuracy on a mouse organogenesis atlas)
Results vary with the underlying commercial LLM and its version
enhanced_abstract.why_it_matters: Rule 3 (algorithm, preferred). The most complete published agent design for annotation, and directly relevant to the group's focus: it was tested on cancer cells and on fine T cell states from the ProjecTILs reference. Its validator, quality score and boost agents are patterns our agent can reuse.

sequencing.summary: Generated new scRNA-seq of brain metastases from non-small cell lung cancer patients (clinical trial NCT03398694); benchmarks otherwise reuse published data.

quantification.summary: Not described in the main text.

preprocessing.summary: Seurat v5 NormalizeData, then FindAllMarkers (min.pct 0.1, adjusted p < 0.05, log2FC > 0.25) to get per-cluster markers; the authors recommend QC, doublet detection and ambient RNA correction first.

dimensionality_reduction.summary: UMAP used only to display results.

clustering.summary: Assumes clustering is done externally; an optional Subclustering agent annotates subclusters of one population together. Future versions may integrate clustering.

annotation.summary: Multi-agent LLM annotation with validation loop, quality scoring, reasoning reports, optional boost, consensus and RAG agents; evaluated with Cell Ontology full/partial/incorrect scoring.
methods: RAG over CellMarker 2.0 and Cell Ontology

trajectory.summary: Noted as a harder case (continuous trajectories weaken marker-based annotation) and a possible future agent task.

algorithms.name: CASSIA multi-agent framework
algorithms.description: Annotator, Validator, Formatter, Scorer and Reporter agents with optional Boost, Subclustering, Consensus and RAG agents.
